winter-1924.summary: Games held as an “International Winter Sports Week” and only later recognized as the first Winter Olympics.
facts: Curling was also contested, but its medals weren't officially recognized until 2006.
Norway and Finland took more than half the medals.

winter-1928.summary: Games where the weather was so warm that some events were canceled.
facts: The skeleton sled event made its debut on the Cresta Run.
A warm foehn wind forced bobsled to be cut from four runs to two.

winter-1932.summary: Games held in the depths of the Great Depression, with only 17 nations taking part.
facts: The cost of crossing the Atlantic kept many athletes from Europe at home.
A medal podium was used at the Olympics for the first time, giving the ceremony its modern look.

winter-1936.summary: The Winter Games the Nazi regime used as a propaganda stage.
facts: Alpine skiing became an official sport for the first time.
Sonja Henie won her third straight Olympic figure skating title.

winter-1948.summary: Games held in a neutral country after a 12-year break caused by the war.
facts: South Korea competed for the first time, sending three speed skaters.
Norway and Sweden finished with identical medal counts, so no single nation could be ranked first.

winter-1952.summary: Games whose torch was lit from the hearth at the birthplace of Norheim, the pioneer of modern skiing.
facts: Hjalmar Andersen of the host nation won three gold medals in speed skating.
Women's cross-country skiing was introduced for the first time.

winter-1956.summary: The first Winter Games televised to multiple countries.
facts: The Soviet Union topped the standings in its very first Winter Games.
A female athlete took the Olympic athletes' oath for the first time.

winter-1960.summary: Games where bobsled was the only sport left out, because no track was built.
facts: Walt Disney staged the opening ceremony.
Biathlon joined the program as an official sport for the first time.

winter-1964.summary: Games so short of snow that soldiers hauled it in from the Brenner Pass.
facts: For the first time, the Winter Games flame was lit at Olympia in Greece.
Luge debuted as an official sport with three events.

winter-1968.summary: The first Games to carry out sex testing and doping tests.
facts: Jean-Claude Killy swept all three alpine skiing events.
Color television coverage began in earnest.

winter-1972.summary: The first Winter Games held outside Europe and North America, in Asia.
facts: The host nation swept the podium in the normal hill ski jump.
An alpine skier was expelled just before the opening for having accepted money.

winter-1976.summary: Games that the same city hosted again after 12 years, when the original host gave them back after a public vote.
facts: Denver, in the United States, withdrew after voters rejected public funding in a 1972 referendum.
To mark its second time as host, both the 1964 cauldron and a new one were lit.

winter-1980.summary: The Games of the “Miracle on Ice,” when a hockey team made up mostly of college players beat the Soviet Union.
facts: Eric Heiden won all five speed skating events.
Artificial snow was laid down for Olympic competition for the first time.

winter-1984.summary: The first Winter Games held in a socialist country.
facts: Eight years later, the city became a battleground in a civil war.
Torvill and Dean received perfect artistic-impression scores from every judge in ice dance.

winter-1988.summary: The Games where the Jamaica bobsled team made its first appearance.
facts: The team's story became the 1993 film “Cool Runnings.”
Ski jumper Eddie Edwards became famous for finishing last.

winter-1992.summary: The last Winter Games held in the same year as the Summer Games.
facts: Kim Ki-hoon won South Korea's first Winter Olympic gold medal, in short track.
A reunified Germany competed as a single team and finished first.

winter-1994.summary: Games held just two years after the previous ones, to stagger the Winter and Summer Games two years apart.
facts: The attack on figure skater Nancy Kerrigan erupted just before the Games.
One ice hockey arena was built inside a cavern carved out of a mountain.

winter-1998.summary: The Games where snowboarding became an official sport for the first time.
facts: Professional ice hockey players took part for the first time.
The host nation won gold in the team ski jump.

winter-2002.summary: Games held after a bidding bribery scandal led to sweeping rule changes.
facts: Kim Dong-sung's disqualification in short track sparked a major controversy.
After judging manipulation in figure skating came to light, gold medals were awarded to two pairs.

winter-2006.summary: Games held in an industrial city at the foot of the Alps, home to Fiat's headquarters.
facts: South Korea won six gold medals in short track.
The torch traveled 11,300 kilometers across Italy over 64 days.

winter-2010.summary: The Games where the host nation won its first gold medal on home soil.
facts: Kim Yuna won figure skating with a world-record score of 228.56.
The host nation won the ice hockey final in overtime.

winter-2014.summary: The most expensive Winter Games ever, held at a subtropical resort.
facts: Systematic doping came to light, and several medals were stripped.
As medals were stripped and restored again and again, the top spot in the gold medal count changed hands several times.

winter-2018.summary: The first Winter Games held in South Korea, with the white tiger Soohorang as mascot.
facts: Athletes from North Korea and South Korea marched together at the opening ceremony.
The women's curling team won silver and became a national sensation.

winter-2022.summary: Games in the first city to have hosted both the Summer and Winter Olympics.
facts: Nearly all the snow at the venues was artificial.
Because of COVID-19, spectators were effectively barred.

winter-2026.summary: Games that carried the names of two cities and were spread across three regions of northern Italy.
facts: Cortina d'Ampezzo hosted the Winter Games again after 70 years.
Klæbo won all six cross-country skiing events, setting the record for most gold medals at a single Winter Games.
